summary: ## Verdict **Do not merge** — this change introduces a critical cross-site scripting (XSS) hole by feeding unsanitized `body` straight into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. ## What went wrong `Comment` previously escaped `&`, `<`, and `>` before assigning HTML. That made the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` path safe for plain text (at the cost of no rich markup). This PR deletes `escapeHtml` and passes `body` through raw. Any comment whose `body` contains HTML or script will execute in the viewer’s origin. Example payload: `` or `` (and many attribute/handler variants). That is classic stored XSS if comments are user-controlled — which a public `Comment` component strongly implies. The comment about “bold/links” does not mitigate this: raw HTML is not markdown. Rich formatting needs a markdown (or subset) parser **plus** a sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify with a tight allowlist), or a React renderer that never uses raw HTML for untrusted input. ## Scope note The repo only contains this component; there is no upstream sanitizer or caller guard visible. The defect is fully introduced in this diff. **Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes escapeHtml and passes unsanitized body into dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so attacker-controlled HTML/JS in comments executes in-page. That is a real stored-XSS regression; critical severity is appropriate.
